correctness.rationale: For unit edges the exact nodal Gram matrix M has diagonal degree/3 and cross entries 1/6. The invariant three-class matrix Q and its inverse determine all evaluation kernels. Exact rational integration gives the displayed five-term norm at each vertex in a largest nonsingleton part. Two sign regimes and exact positive-coefficient rational-polynomial identities establish strict competition with the other vertex classes; convexity plus sign opposition excludes all interiors. A second set of universal coefficient identities yields the exact cutoff \(q=4\), while a rational limit yields 7/3. The delivered checker executes these symbolic identities and 28 independent exact matrix evaluations; finite checks alone are not invoked as proof.

value.rationale: The exact L-infinity stability/positivity-amplification problem on unit metric complete tripartite networks with two independent classes is natural after classical spline projection work. The full two-parameter family has a nontrivial sign-switching Gram kernel and requires four universal polynomial dominance identities. A universal threshold depending only on the largest class size, complete norming-location classification, and explicit extremizing inputs are concrete structure rather than a routine isolated numeric calculation.
